key_insight: A PICNN trained on finite-volume residuals can serve as the prediction step in a physics-preserving two-phase flow solver while retaining thermodynamic consistency, mass conservation, and boundedness after correction.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate for porous-media flow simulations, especially where discontinuous permeability and interfacial flux continuity make standard PINNs less reliable.
method: PICNN learns cell-local flow predictions from finite-volume residuals
Interfacial fluxes are computed with TPFA using neighboring cell-centered values
A post-processing correction enforces energy stability, mass conservation, and bounds
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results showing the finite-volume-residual-trained PICNN can replace the traditional prediction solver within the physics-preserving framework and outperform conventional PINNs in capturing local interactions.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate finite-volume residual formulation and correction design, especially for highly heterogeneous porous media.
paper_title: The PICNN-Assisted Physics-Preserving Scheme for Thermodynamically Consistent Two-Phase Flow in Porous Media
